identity.headline: Software Engineer, React and TypeScript
identity.work_authorization: Ghanaian citizen. Available for fully remote roles worldwide and on-site roles in Accra. Open to visa sponsorship conversations.
identity.availability: Available from November 2026, when national service ends.

narrative.summary: Software engineer building production React and TypeScript applications. At AmaliTech I am a core frontend engineer on an enterprise office management platform used across multiple offices, working in a Turborepo monorepo with TanStack Query, Zustand, full localisation and an end to end test suite. I also founded SLINT Tech, a nonprofit widening access to technology in Ghana.
narrative.positioning: I am early in my career and deliberately deep rather than broad. I focus on React, TypeScript, and the craft of interfaces that hold up in production, with enough backend and cloud to own a feature from database to pixel.
narrative.mission: To create a tech ecosystem where talent thrives regardless of gender, background, or circumstance.
narrative.story_line: Raised by my mother and grandmother, I learned that strength is consistency. Technology became the language through which I could build, solve and empower, which is why I founded SLINT Tech alongside my engineering work.
differentiators: Ships production software inside a real engineering team: an enterprise platform in a monorepo, with code review, CI, German and French localisation and Playwright end to end tests.
Best Female Student in STEM at ATU and Outstanding Student of the Year at COMPSSA, while holding a 4.30 of 5.00 GPA.
Studying BSc Applied Artificial Intelligence alongside a BTech in Computer Science and full time work.
Founded and runs SLINT Tech, mentoring new developers, which is direct evidence of ownership and follow through.
narrative.why_me_closing: I would welcome the chance to talk about where a frontend engineer who ships carefully and learns quickly could add the most value to your team.

bullets: Work as a core frontend engineer on an enterprise office management platform used across multiple offices, delivering attendance, floor plan seating, user management, remote day and out of office requests in a Turborepo monorepo.
Built the interactive floor plan seating with a live availability map, seat booking flows and admin configuration of floors, zones and seats.
Delivered the manager approval workflow, an in app notifications inbox with grouping and unread badges, and the super admin user management module with role filtering and access gating.
Integrated the frontend with backend REST APIs using Axios and TanStack Query, owned the frontend to backend API contract, and used MSW to mock endpoints for local development and testing.
Added German and French localisation with CI enforced key parity validation, and wrote unit, component and end to end tests with Vitest, React Testing Library, MSW and Playwright.
Launched and scaled a nonprofit technology organisation focused on bridging the digital skills gap.
Led recruitment, training programmes and team coordination across career paths.
Built a learning culture and community support systems for junior developers.
Built, customised and maintained WordPress websites, ensuring responsive design and plugin integration.
Wrote custom CSS, HTML, JavaScript and PHP to implement tailored layouts, responsive components and interactive features beyond default theme capabilities.
Supported system maintenance, user troubleshooting and technical documentation.
Worked alongside senior IT staff to improve service delivery and uptime.

outreach.tone: Warm, direct and specific. Confident without overclaiming. Never generic flattery, never buzzword stacking. Short sentences. British spelling.
never_claim: years of experience I do not have
technologies not listed in my skills
prior employment at companies I have not worked for

banned_phrases: I hope this email finds you well
at the end of the day
I believe I would be a great fit
rules: Never use an em dash or en dash. Use a comma, a full stop, or a colon instead.
Every letter must name at least one concrete detail from the job description, and one concrete artefact from my work with a number, a technology or a link.
No sentence may be true of any other applicant. Cut anything that would survive a find and replace of the company name.
Maximum 220 words in an outreach email body. Maximum 320 words in a cover letter body.
Never open with a greeting about hoping the reader is well.
Never claim seniority, years of experience, or technologies not in my skills list.
British spelling. Plain words over corporate vocabulary.
